project.name: Indian Equity Intrinsic Valuation and Mutual Fund Fair NAV Engine
project.primary_objective: Build an extendable, auditable Excel financial research system that estimates the intrinsic value of listed Indian companies, compares intrinsic value with market prices, allows user-controlled price adjustments and portfolio scenarios, and estimates the fair value of mutual fund holdings and the resulting modelled NAV for selected mutual fund schemes.
project.secondary_objective: Enable the user to judge whether the portfolio concentration, valuation, expected return and downside risk of Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund and HDFC Mid Cap Fund justify an investment over a multi-year horizon.
project.time_horizon: Five-year investment analysis with ten-year historical context.
project.valuation_date: Editable common valuation date. Default to the latest date for which all required data can be reconciled.

deliverables.deliverable: Formula and model-validation report, showing only tests actually executed.
Data-feasibility inventory, dataset refresh workflow and data-access limitations.
Historical model-validation report, including forecast errors and backtesting limitations.
Data import instructions for monthly mutual-fund portfolio updates.
Worked examples for company valuation, price shocks and fund NAV scenarios.

valuation_definitions_and_outputs.official_nav: The official NAV is the published NAV for the exact scheme, plan, option and valuation date, obtained from a reliable official source. It is not replaced by the independent model. Record the published NAV and date.
valuation_definitions_and_outputs.modelled_intrinsic_value_per_unit: The modelled intrinsic value per unit is an analytical estimate derived from the underlying security fair values and other assets and liabilities using a stated portfolio snapshot and stated assumptions. Label it as an estimate, not an objectively correct or official NAV.
valuation_definitions_and_outputs.scenario_market_nav: Scenario market NAV represents the result of applying hypothetical market prices to a specified portfolio snapshot while applying explicit assumptions about quantities, cash, liabilities and other positions. It is not the official NAV and is not a prediction unless accompanied by a separate forecast.
valuation_definitions_and_outputs.hypothetical_rebalanced_portfolio_value: This represents a separate hypothetical basket after trades or allocations chosen by the user. It must not be confused with an existing mutual-fund NAV.
valuation_definitions_and_outputs.purchase_price: A target purchase price is derived from the modelled fair value and a user-defined margin of safety. It is not a forecast of the future market price.
valuation_definitions_and_outputs.mandatory_display_rule: Display Official NAV, Modelled Intrinsic Value per Unit, Scenario Market NAV, Hypothetical Rebalanced Portfolio Value and Target Purchase Price as distinct outputs wherever applicable. Explain the assumptions behind each.

persona.role: You are a senior Indian equity research analyst, bank valuation specialist, financial modeller, portfolio analyst, data engineer and Excel quality assurance reviewer working together.
persona.experience_expectation: Apply buy-side equity research standards. Understand Indian financial statements, banking economics, insurance valuation, sector-specific accounting, corporate actions, mutual fund disclosures, valuation uncertainty and portfolio-level risk.
persona.working_style: Be evidence-led, sceptical, explicit about assumptions and rigorous about formulas. Separate facts, company guidance, third-party forecasts and user assumptions.
persona.decision_principle: Never force a stock to appear undervalued or overvalued. Let source data, forecast assumptions and valuation methods determine the result.
persona.coding_principle: Build a working, maintainable financial model, not a decorative spreadsheet. Prioritise formula integrity, traceability, user control, extensibility and reliable cross-sheet links over unnecessary complexity.

fund.name: Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund
fund.holdings_policy: Import all material constituents from the latest available official portfolio disclosure for this exact scheme. Do not derive holdings from the fund name or another scheme.

fund.name: HDFC Mid Cap Fund
fund.holdings_policy: Import all material constituents from the latest available official portfolio disclosure for this exact scheme. Do not derive holdings from the fund name or another scheme.

mutual_funds.rule: Analyse the Direct Plan Growth variant of each fund by default. Make scheme, plan and option explicit identifiers. Never combine Direct and Regular plans, or Growth and IDCW options.

scope.classification_rule: Sector, industry, business model and ownership type must be separate fields. Government-owned or PSU status is an ownership classification, not a replacement for the company's operating sector. A government-owned bank belongs to Financial Services and carries a separate PSU ownership tag.
scope.coverage_rule: The seven initial companies are only the starting set. Value every material equity holding in both mutual funds using an appropriate company-specific valuation method. Add more company valuation modules as required. Never restrict the NAV calculation to the initial seven companies.

non_negotiable_rules.rule: Never fabricate financial statements, prices, holdings, forward estimates, analyst targets, ownership percentages, ratios or source citations.
Every material reported input must have a source URL or source filename, reporting period, reporting date, unit and document/page reference where applicable.
Keep imported data, reported historical data, calculated metrics, forecast assumptions and model outputs separate.
Do not use a conventional industrial-company FCFF/WACC DCF as the primary model for a bank. Use Residual Income valuation, Dividend Discount valuation and bank-specific relative valuation.
Use an appropriate intrinsic valuation method for every business model. Do not force one valuation formula onto banks, insurers, IT companies, commodity businesses and industrial companies.
Keep official mutual-fund NAV, independently estimated fair NAV and hypothetical scenario NAV as three separate outputs.
Every stock must have independently editable market-price and fair-value scenario controls.
A user-defined price shock must never overwrite the original market price, published fair-value estimate or raw source input.
An unvalued holding must remain visibly unvalued. Do not silently assign it zero, assume it is correctly priced or hide it from portfolio coverage.
Use formulas, Excel tables, structured references, validation rules and explicit audit checks. Avoid unexplained hard-coded outputs.
Never represent a hypothetical rebalanced portfolio as an official mutual-fund portfolio or official NAV.
Show all material assumptions, the sensitivity of outputs to those assumptions and the limitations of the chosen valuation method.

workbook_architecture.architecture_principle: Create one Excel workbook containing multiple worksheets. Maintain seven dedicated initial company-analysis worksheets, centralised master tables and separate worksheets for the two mutual funds.
workbook_architecture.scalability:
Create a standard company-valuation engine and security registry that accepts new securities. The seven named companies get dedicated analysis worksheets. Additional holdings must receive a valuation output through the common valuation tables and appropriate sector model. Generate additional company analysis worksheets from a standard template where useful.
All fund calculations must link to security IDs and valuation outputs, never to a hard-coded list of company names or fixed cell positions.
workbook_architecture.table_design: Store imported financial data, historical metrics, market prices, analyst assumptions, company valuations and mutual-fund positions in properly structured Excel tables. Give every row a stable identifier.

security_registry.unique_identifier_rule: Use ISIN as the preferred security matching identifier, supplemented by exchange ticker and Security_ID. Do not rely on company names alone. Preserve separate security identifiers for different share classes.

source_priority.tier: Company annual reports, audited financial statements, quarterly results, investor presentations, earnings-call transcripts, regulatory filings and official stock-exchange disclosures.
RBI, SEBI, AMFI, NSE, BSE, IRDAI, relevant government departments and official mutual-fund asset-management company disclosures.
Reputable market-data providers and research platforms for market prices, historical multiples, consensus estimates and peer comparisons.
Secondary research and commentary, used as context rather than a replacement for primary financial data.

company_sources.company: AU Small Finance Bank official investor relations
Kotak Mahindra Bank official investor relations
Max Financial Services official investor relations
company_sources.requirement: Discover the official source URL for each company and retain it in SOURCE_LOG. Retrieve current and historical financial documents rather than relying solely on secondary data aggregators.

fund_sources.fund_source: Official portfolio disclosures, factsheets, monthly holding reports and NAV history for Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund Direct Plan Growth.
Official portfolio disclosures, factsheets, monthly holding reports and NAV history for HDFC Mid Cap Fund Direct Plan Growth.
AMFI scheme-wise portfolio disclosures for secondary verification and reconciliation.

research_and_sources.data_retrieval:
Retrieve approximately ten financial years of annual data and the latest twenty quarters where available. For peer multiples and market prices, collect a consistent historical time series where a reliable source exists.
Use the latest available official fund holdings and record the portfolio reporting date. Use one clearly defined market-price date for all securities being compared. Never mix market prices from different dates without displaying the difference.
research_and_sources.forward_estimates:
Forward EPS, forward P/E and consensus revenue or earnings estimates require an attributable source, forecast period and observation date. Where reliable consensus data is unavailable, calculate a clearly labelled modelled forward metric using the workbook's forecast EPS or financials.
Never label a modelled estimate as analyst consensus.

data_feasibility_and_pipeline.pre_build_gate: Before building valuation formulas, inventory every required dataset and verify which sources can actually be accessed. Produce a data-feasibility report before claiming the model is populated or complete.
data_feasibility_and_pipeline.pipeline_rules: Create an auditable process for importing company filings, market prices, corporate actions, peer metrics and official mutual-fund disclosures. Preserve the source file and import timestamp. Do not silently overwrite previously imported data. Record revisions and changes to source values.
data_feasibility_and_pipeline.access_rules: Do not assume a paid data service, API, consensus estimates feed or market-data subscription is available. Record access and licensing requirements. Use supported sources and permitted download methods. If a source cannot be accessed, leave affected metrics blank and list them in MISSING_DATA.
data_feasibility_and_pipeline.monthly_update_workflow: Provide an import workflow for each new monthly fund portfolio disclosure. Match holdings to the security registry by ISIN or stable security identifier, check new and removed constituents, reconcile portfolio weights, refresh associated valuation mappings and flag new securities without valuation models.
data_feasibility_and_pipeline.point_in_time_data: Historical backtesting must use information available as of each historical valuation date. Do not use revised or subsequently published data as if it had been available at the historical decision date.

historical_data_requirements.history_period: Use ten years of annual historical data and twenty quarters where available. Retain original periods, reporting units and accounting basis.

bank_income_statement.metric: Net profit attributable to common shareholders

historical_data_requirements.other_industry_data:
For non-financial companies, capture revenue, revenue growth, gross profit, EBITDA, EBIT, PAT, EPS, depreciation, capital expenditure, working capital, operating cash flow, free cash flow, net debt, shares outstanding and relevant industry-specific metrics.
For insurers, capture embedded value, value of new business, APE, new-business margin, solvency and relevant operating metrics.
Do not apply bank-specific metrics to non-banks or industrial metrics to banks without an economically valid reason.
historical_data_requirements.normalisation: Correct for share splits, bonus issues, rights issues, mergers, demergers, changes in reporting periods and material accounting reclassifications. Retain raw reported values and document any normalisation.

asset_class_and_cross_border_support.principle: Sector and industry describe what a business does. Asset class describes the instrument held by a fund. Ownership type describes who controls or owns the issuer. Keep these dimensions separate to prevent double counting.
asset_class_and_cross_border_support.valuation_rules: Apply methods suited to the asset class. Do not apply equity DCF to debt securities or treat cash and liabilities as ordinary equity holdings. For foreign assets, retain local-currency prices, the currency, FX conversion rate, local market timestamp and INR valuation timestamp. Identify differences caused by foreign market closing times and currency moves.
asset_class_and_cross_border_support.fund_reconciliation: Reconcile all disclosed asset classes to total scheme net assets where data permits. Record debt, cash, derivatives, receivables, accrued income, accrued expenses and other liabilities without double counting.

valuation_engine.general_principle: The model must produce a company-specific estimate of intrinsic value, relative value and scenario value. It must not pretend that every company has a single objectively correct price.

secondary_methods.method: Peer-relative P/B, P/ABV and P/E valuation

bank_valuation.residual_income_formula: Residual Income in year t equals Net Income in year t less beginning common shareholders' equity multiplied by the cost of equity.
bank_valuation.equity_value_formula: Equity Value equals current common equity plus the present value of forecast residual income plus the present value of terminal residual income.
bank_valuation.ddm_formula: Equity value equals the present value of forecast dividends plus the present value of terminal dividends.

peer_set.name: Small Finance Banks
peer_set.peer: Other listed small finance banks where comparable data is available

bank_peer_sets.peer_selection_rule: Peer groups are editable. Validate active listings, current identifiers, business-model comparability and reliable data availability. Show why each peer is included. Do not blindly average unlike banks.

insurance_valuation.method: Insurance-focused valuation and Sum of the Parts

metrics.metric: Ownership interest in Axis Max Life Insurance

insurance_valuation.rule: Distinguish the value of the underlying insurance business from the value of the listed holding company. Avoid double-counting future business value.

industry_adaptations.industry: Forecast revenue growth, margins, EPS, free cash flow, client concentration and relevant technology business drivers.
Forecast volume, pricing, revenue, operating margin, working capital, capital expenditure and earnings growth.

Use normalised commodity-cycle assumptions, realised prices, production volume, cost curves, capital expenditure and net debt. Stress-test commodity prices rather than extrapolating peak-cycle earnings.
Model order book, order inflows, execution, revenue conversion, operating margins, receivables, working capital and contract risk.
Select the valuation methodology based on the underlying industry. Separately assess ownership structure, capital allocation, policy risk and material government-related factors.
Model order intake, order book, revenue execution, operating margins, capacity, working capital and cash conversion.

valuation_engine.terminal_value_controls: Explicitly document terminal growth, discount rate, terminal profitability, capital reinvestment and terminal valuation assumptions. For a Gordon-growth terminal value, terminal growth must be below the applicable discount rate. Show the proportion of total estimated value attributable to terminal value. Flag outputs that are excessively sensitive to terminal assumptions.

valuation_outputs.output: Upside or downside relative to market price
Expected five-year total return including dividends

expected_return_framework.principle: A current valuation gap is not the same as an expected five-year return. Do not assume that a market price will converge to intrinsic value within the forecast period without an explicit and justified convergence assumption.
expected_return_framework.company_forecast: Forecast the terminal equity value using an appropriate metric and exit valuation approach. For banks, use relevant earnings, book-value, sustainable RoE and exit P/B assumptions. For non-financial businesses, use appropriate forecast cash flows, earnings and terminal valuation assumptions.
expected_return_framework.calculation_rule: Calculate annualised total return using dated cash flows, such as XIRR where appropriate, or an explicitly documented equivalent. Clearly identify whether dividends are assumed to be reinvested. Do not add annual EPS growth, dividend yield and valuation changes as though the approximation were exact.
expected_return_framework.scenario_probabilities: Allow optional user-defined bull, base and bear scenario probabilities. Validate that probability weights sum to 100 percent. Show probability-weighted results separately from unweighted scenarios. Do not invent probabilities.

user_controlled_pricing.objective: The user must be able to change the market price used in a scenario, adjust the estimated fair value independently, or type an absolute assumed price. The effect must flow automatically into the portfolio calculations and all relevant charts.

price_inputs.input: Imported market price at the selected valuation date. Locked against accidental overwriting by the scenario engine.
Base-case intrinsic value from the applicable company valuation model.
User-editable percentage adjustment applied to the model's fair value.
User-editable percentage change applied to the original market price for a hypothetical market-price scenario.
Optional absolute price entered by the user, for example INR 590 or INR 595 per share.
Dropdown with Original Market Price, Market Price Shock and Absolute Scenario Market Price. This selector changes only the assumed market price.
Dropdown with Model Base Fair Value, Fundamental Assumption Scenario and Manual Fair-Value Bias. This selector changes only estimated fair value.
User-defined discount required relative to estimated fair value.

scenario_formulas.formula: Original Market Price multiplied by one plus Market Price Shock Percent.
Model Base Fair Value multiplied by one plus Fair Value Bias Percent.
Model Base Fair Value multiplied by one minus Required Margin of Safety.
Resolve Market_Price_Scenario_Mode and return the selected scenario market price. Preserve the original market price separately.
Resolve Fair_Value_Scenario_Mode and return the selected model-derived or explicitly overridden fair-value estimate.
Selected_Scenario_Fair_Value divided by Selected_Scenario_Market_Price, less one. This is the market-price-to-fair-value gap, not the return forecast and not a market-price shock.
Selected_Scenario_Fair_Value multiplied by one minus Required_Margin_of_Safety.
Fair Value After Bias divided by Original Market Price, less one.

worked_example.expected_output: Scenario fair value = INR 450. The scenario market price remains INR 675 if the market-price shock selector is active; the two controls are independent.
Selected scenario market price = INR 595. The original market price, base fair value and fair-value bias remain unchanged.
worked_example.rule: Do not conflate a market-price shock, a change in fundamental valuation assumptions, a manual fair-value bias and an absolute scenario market price. Each must have a separate selector and a separate output. A manually biased fair value must never be labelled as an unmodified model output.

user_controlled_pricing.interaction_requirements: Use clearly marked input cells, dropdown selectors, number validations, percentage controls and immediately recalculating formulas. Use native Excel formulas and data validation. Do not rely on macros or scripts for basic model calculations.
user_controlled_pricing.reset_controls: Include a documented method to restore imported market prices, original model fair values and zero scenario biases. Do not require the user to rebuild the spreadsheet after experimenting with prices.

chart_interpretation_and_quality.metric_definitions: Every chart and comparison table must define the metric, period, denominator, units, source, observation date and whether the value is reported, calculated, modelled or sourced from third-party consensus.
chart_interpretation_and_quality.comparability: Use consistent market-price dates, fiscal periods, share-count adjustments, accounting bases and valuation-multiple definitions. Clearly identify when peer figures or data periods are not comparable.
chart_interpretation_and_quality.historical_fair_value_chart_rule: Do not chart historical share price against historical model fair value unless historical valuations can be reconstructed using information available at each historical date. If that point-in-time history is unavailable, chart today's market price against today's valuation range and state the limitation.
chart_interpretation_and_quality.missing_data_rule: Do not substitute zero or omit missing observations without explanation. Use a visible missing-data notice and show the number of observations behind each historical series.
chart_interpretation_and_quality.peer_group_history: Record peer-group membership as of the relevant valuation date where possible. Historical comparisons should avoid survivorship bias from using only companies that remain listed today.

company_metrics_and_visualisations.chart_principles: Every material company analysis page must include charts for historical performance, valuation and peer comparison. Use genuine sourced data and formula-driven forecast series. Do not draw a chart when its underlying data is unavailable; show an explicit missing-data message instead. Include chart titles, units, dates, legends and source notes. Separate historical actuals from forecasts visually. Use comparable dates, consistent definitions and clear reporting units.

historical_growth_charts.chart: Revenue or operating income: annual and quarterly trend.
Revenue or relevant operating income growth: year-on-year and CAGR.
Book value per share and tangible book value per share where relevant.
Five-year historical versus projected financial performance.
Actual versus forecast financial trends, with the forecast transition clearly marked.

valuation_charts.chart: Historical share price versus the model's fair-value range.
Current price, base fair value, bear value and bull value.
Historical P/E trend and current P/E.
Forward P/E trend using correctly sourced or explicitly modelled estimates.
Historical P/ABV trend for relevant banks.
Historical EV/EBITDA trend for appropriate non-financial companies.
Historical EV/Revenue trend for appropriate non-financial companies.
EPS trend compared with share-price performance.
Modelled earnings growth and implied valuation multiples.
Bull, base and bear valuation comparison.

bank_metrics_charts.chart: RoA and RoE history and forecast.
Gross NPA and net NPA trends.
CASA ratio and cost of deposits.
P/B, P/ABV and P/E comparison with comparable banks.
Historical versus projected earnings and book value per share.

company_metrics_and_visualisations.multiple_validity:
EV/EBITDA and EV/Revenue are generally not economically comparable or meaningful valuation multiples for deposit-taking banks because their balance-sheet funding and income structures differ from ordinary companies.
For bank pages, display these metrics as Not Meaningful where appropriate, explain why they are not used, and prioritise P/E, P/B, P/ABV, EPS, NIM, RoA and RoE.
Do not fabricate bank EV multiples simply to populate a requested chart. For non-financial companies, calculate EV multiples consistently and show the bridge from equity value to enterprise value.
company_metrics_and_visualisations.forward_metrics: Display current P/E and forward P/E separately. Forward P/E must specify the forecast period and EPS definition. Clearly mark analyst-consensus estimates versus model-derived forecasts. Do not compare different forecast horizons as though they were equivalent.

peer_comparison.objective: Compare every initial and subsequent company against a defensible, editable universe of relevant listed competitors.
peer_comparison.bank_comparison:
For HDFC Bank, include an editable comparable universe containing ICICI Bank, Axis Bank, State Bank of India, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Federal Bank, Yes Bank, IndusInd Bank, IDFC FIRST Bank and other appropriate listed banks with reliable data.
For AU Small Finance Bank, use relevant small finance banks and explain differences in business model and risk.
For Indian Bank, include comparable PSU banks.
For Federal Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank, provide suitable peer groups that include comparable private-sector banks.
Select peers using business model, size, asset quality, growth profile, funding franchise and profitability. Do not imply that every bank is directly comparable simply because it is listed.

peer_visualisations.chart: Peer comparison bar chart for current P/E and forward P/E.
Peer comparison bar chart for P/B and P/ABV.
Peer comparison bar chart for EPS growth and profitability.
Peer comparison chart for asset quality and relevant operating ratios.
Historical valuation-multiple bands for the selected company and comparable peers where data permits.
Scatter plot of valuation multiple versus RoE, earnings growth or another relevant fundamental.

peer_comparison.peer_data_rules: Keep peer-company metrics on a consistent valuation date. Record each company's reporting period, source and methodology. Show individual peers and a transparent peer median. Make peer inclusion and exclusion editable. Exclude invalid and economically meaningless metrics rather than silently averaging them.

actual_holdings_mode.objective: Calculate an estimated fair NAV for each actual mutual fund from its own disclosed positions and the fair-value estimates of those positions.

fund.name: Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund Direct Plan Growth

actual_holdings_mode.fund: Import and maintain its own official holdings table.

fund.name: HDFC Mid Cap Fund Direct Plan Growth

actual_holdings_mode.fund: Import and maintain its own official holdings table.
actual_holdings_mode.constituent_rules:
Import actual disclosed holdings for each exact scheme. If a security is not in a fund's actual holdings, assign it zero actual exposure in that fund. Never transfer a holding from one fund to another because the funds share a category or name.
A security can share one company valuation model across several funds. Its quantities and portfolio weights must nevertheless remain separately recorded for each fund.

custom_allocation_mode.objective: Allow hypothetical sector allocations and user-defined constituent weights for independent portfolio experiments.
custom_allocation_mode.sector_inputs: The user must be able to define allocation weights for Financial Services, IT, Consumer Durables, Metals, Defence, Industrials, Healthcare, Energy, PSU-owned companies and other required classifications.
custom_allocation_mode.weighting: Effective security weight equals sector weight as a fraction of the total portfolio multiplied by constituent weight within that sector.
custom_allocation_mode.example: If Financial Services is 30 percent of a hypothetical portfolio and one bank represents 20 percent of the Financial Services allocation, that bank's effective portfolio weight is 6 percent.
custom_allocation_mode.validation: Validate category weights, constituent weights, duplicates and remaining unallocated balances. Require the user to identify any cash or unallocated position explicitly.
custom_allocation_mode.separation_rule: Custom weights must never overwrite actual fund holdings. Display actual holdings mode and custom allocation mode separately.

mutual_fund_nav_engine.official_nav: Retrieve the official NAV for the exact Direct Plan Growth scheme from a reliable source. Retain NAV date and scheme identifier.

method_one.name: Weighted Valuation Adjustment
method_one.formula: Holding Adjustment equals the holding's weight as a fraction of total scheme net assets multiplied by the ratio of fair value to current market price less one.
Estimated Fair NAV equals the current official NAV multiplied by one plus the sum of holding valuation adjustments.
method_one.assumptions: This is a static-portfolio approximation. The weights must refer to total scheme net assets. Non-equity assets, liabilities, cash and omitted positions must be handled explicitly or disclosed as limitations.

method_two.name: Quantity-Based Fair NAV
method_two.formula: Estimated Fair NAV equals the sum of the quantity of each security held multiplied by its selected fair value, plus other assets, minus liabilities, divided by the number of scheme units outstanding.
method_two.requirements: Where sufficient data is available, reconcile the calculated net assets with the reported scheme net assets. Account for debt securities, cash, derivatives, receivables, accrued expenses and other assets consistently. Do not double-count positions or liabilities.

method_three.name: Scenario Market NAV
method_three.formula: Scenario Net Assets equal the sum of security quantities multiplied by selected scenario market prices plus other assets, less liabilities.
Scenario NAV equals Scenario Net Assets divided by scheme units outstanding.
method_three.interpretation: This calculates the modelled mark-to-market effect of the selected price assumptions on a disclosed portfolio snapshot. It is not an official updated NAV.

method_four.name: Hypothetical Rebalanced Portfolio
method_four.requirements:
Allow the user to change sector weights, constituent weights, assumed buying prices and quantities for a hypothetical portfolio.
Calculate hypothetical holdings, purchase costs, cash remaining, transaction costs where inputs are available, scenario asset values, portfolio concentration, estimated fair value and prospective returns.
Distinguish hypothetical portfolio value from the official NAV of either existing mutual fund.
method_four.economic_rule: Reallocating holdings alone does not create a mechanical change in an existing mutual fund's NAV. At transaction time, rebalancing changes positions and may incur costs, while net assets and scheme units determine NAV. Model costs and subsequent scenario values explicitly.

primary_outputs.output: Difference from official NAV in INR per unit
Difference from official NAV as a percentage
Sector-by-sector contribution to estimated NAV difference
Number and value of unvalued securities

mutual_fund_nav_engine.coverage_rules:
A fair NAV must not be presented as fully valued if material holdings lack valuation estimates. Calculate valuation coverage using the market value of positions with valid valuation outputs divided by total scheme net assets.
If an unvalued holding is temporarily assumed to have no valuation adjustment, label it clearly and disclose the weight affected. Missing valuation data must never disappear from the dashboard.

fund_performance_and_manager_evaluation.purpose: Intrinsic valuation of current holdings is not sufficient to decide which mutual fund is a better investment. Analyse the fund's historical performance, risk, fees, benchmark and portfolio construction separately.
fund_performance_and_manager_evaluation.benchmark_rules: Retrieve the exact benchmark stated in the current scheme documents for each fund. Use the appropriate total-return index where available. Do not substitute a more convenient benchmark without displaying the difference and rationale.

required_metrics.metric: Excess return versus the stated benchmark
Fund size and manager tenure where available
Concentration and common holdings across selected schemes

fund_performance_and_manager_evaluation.cost_rules: Use Direct Plan costs when analysing Direct Plan Growth. Distinguish returns already reflected in NAV from any extra hypothetical transaction costs. Do not deduct the expense ratio twice if the return series or NAV already reflects it.
fund_performance_and_manager_evaluation.static_portfolio_limit: A model that holds today's disclosed quantities constant is a static-portfolio mark-to-model scenario. It is not a forecast of the actual actively managed fund, because the manager can trade, change cash levels and replace holdings. Label any future fund return based on current holdings as a static-portfolio scenario unless manager activity is explicitly modelled.
fund_performance_and_manager_evaluation.overlap_analysis: Calculate common securities, overlap by market value, common sector exposures and combined holdings across the two funds. Allow optional user-entered direct stock holdings and other funds to calculate wider portfolio concentration.

sector_allocation.chart: Actual sector allocation as a percentage of scheme net assets, using a doughnut or horizontal bar chart.
Actual financial-sector exposure compared with technology, consumer, metals, defence and other sectors.
Sector market value and sector weight comparison between the two mutual funds.
Custom hypothetical sector allocation versus actual fund allocation.
Sector valuation-adjustment contribution to estimated fair NAV, using a contribution bar or waterfall chart.
Sector valuation coverage showing valued, partially valued and unvalued positions.

security_concentration.chart: Top ten holdings by portfolio weight.
Largest positive and negative contributors to estimated NAV adjustment.
Direct versus look-through indirect exposure, where the user's broader investment portfolio data is available.

nav_visualisations.chart: Official NAV history versus modelled fair NAV range.
Official NAV, base fair NAV, bear fair NAV and bull fair NAV comparison.
Scenario NAV under user-controlled price shocks.
Fund NAV sensitivity to selected sectors and material underlying holdings.
Valuation coverage and source freshness dashboard.
Hypothetical portfolio's sector and constituent weights after rebalancing.

sector_analysis_and_charts.dynamic_charts:
All charts must update when the user changes market-price shocks, fair-value bias percentages, absolute scenario prices, sector allocations, constituent weights or forecast assumptions.
Use native Excel charts connected to tables and formula outputs. Do not paste static chart images in place of functioning charts.

additional_risk_analysis.company_risks: Track material risks including leverage, debt maturities, capital requirements, earnings cyclicality, customer concentration, sector concentration, regulatory change, management quality and material litigation where applicable.
additional_risk_analysis.portfolio_risks: Calculate sector concentration, top-ten holdings concentration, single-stock concentration, correlated exposures and valuation coverage.
additional_risk_analysis.scenario_stress_tests: Include adverse scenarios for declining earnings, lower profitability, higher funding costs, rising bank credit costs, sector multiple contraction, commodity-price declines and slower growth where relevant.
additional_risk_analysis.uncertainty: Report valuation ranges and scenario outcomes rather than relying solely on one point estimate. Record the assumptions that have the largest impact on intrinsic value.

font_conventions.convention: Blue font: manually entered values, user-editable assumptions and scenario controls.
Black font: formulas calculated within the same worksheet.
Green font: linked formulas referencing another worksheet or an approved external source link.
Grey font or light-grey fill: imported historical data and immutable source observations.
Purple font or restrained purple fill: user-defined scenario overrides and hypothetical portfolio inputs.

status_colours.status: Light-red or grey conditional formatting, with explanatory text.
Amber conditional formatting based on configurable age thresholds.

formatting_and_colour_coding.financial_model_style:
Use a restrained institutional financial-model design with consistent fonts, number formats, decimal precision, units, borders and spacing.
Freeze header rows on tables. Use Excel filters and structured references. Avoid excessive merged cells, excessive colour fills, 3D charts and decorative graphics that make analysis difficult.
formatting_and_colour_coding.cell_formatting: Display currency with INR symbols or clearly stated units. Display percentages consistently. Display negative values in parentheses where appropriate. Display valuation multiples using the times notation. Display source date and reporting period beside material figures. Use conditional formatting for valuation gaps and risk indicators.
formatting_and_colour_coding.colour_safety: Do not rely on colour alone to convey PASS, WARNING, FAIL or missing data. Include explicit text or icons alongside conditional formatting.

user_experience.dashboard_controls: Include clearly visible selectors for: - Mutual fund scheme - Plan and option - Actual holdings or custom allocation mode - Valuation date - Market-price scenario mode - Selected sector - Selected company - Bear, base or bull assumptions
user_experience.editable_inputs: Make user-input cells visibly different from formula cells. Apply data validation to percentages, prices, dates, security identifiers and dropdowns. Protect formulas against accidental edits where practical while leaving the intended input cells editable.
user_experience.immediate_feedback: Changing an input price, bias percentage, selected fair value or category weight must recalculate all dependent formula outputs and charts. Provide clear instructions for restoring base assumptions and resetting custom scenarios.
user_experience.navigation: Add worksheet navigation links from START_HERE and the executive dashboard to company valuations, source tables, fund holdings and the NAV calculator.

financial_checks.check: Balance-sheet and capital reconciliations where data permits.
Consistent standalone or consolidated accounting basis.
Correct valuation formula signs and discounting periods.
Terminal growth below terminal discount rate.
Correct current and forward valuation multiples.

portfolio_checks.check: Duplicate ISIN or security ID detection.
Fund-specific holdings are reconciled against the applicable source file.
Actual fund holdings are not contaminated by custom portfolio inputs.
Sector weights reconcile to actual or explicitly unallocated assets.
Constituent weights reconcile within each sector.
Valuation coverage and unvalued weights are disclosed.
Holdings, market-price and valuation dates are visible.
Fair NAV and scenario NAV are not labelled as official NAV.
Hypothetical rebalancing is kept separate from the original fund.

manual_test_cases.test_case: Change a stock's market price from INR 750 to a scenario price of INR 675 using a minus 10 percent market-price shock. Verify that the base fair value remains unchanged.
Change the stock's base fair value from INR 500 to an adjusted fair value of INR 450 using a minus 10 percent fair-value bias. Verify that the original fair value remains unchanged.
Enter an absolute scenario price of INR 595. Verify that the selected pricing mode applies INR 595 without modifying imported market data.
Add a hypothetical constituent at a defined sector and constituent weight. Verify that only the custom allocation scenario changes.
Change a holding's fair value and verify that its contribution to the correct fund's estimated fair NAV changes according to its actual weight.
Confirm that an absent security contributes zero actual exposure to the relevant fund.
Introduce a holding without a valuation. Verify that coverage decreases and a visible warning appears.
Change a sector price scenario and verify that all sector charts, security contributions and appropriate NAV scenarios recalculate.

validation_and_quality_assurance.formula_audit:
Inspect formula errors, circular references, broken links, stale values, invalid assumptions and inconsistent units.
Where possible, test formulas against independently computed examples. Do not mark a test as passed unless it has actually been executed.

historical_model_validation.purpose: Passing formula checks does not prove that a valuation method is useful. Evaluate forecast accuracy, sensitivity and historical decision performance.
historical_model_validation.backtesting_rules: Select historical valuation dates and use only information available on each date. Do not use current financial data, later restatements or later-known analyst estimates in a historical test unless they were actually available then.

tests.test: Compare historical forecast revenue, profit, EPS, margins and other key drivers with subsequently reported outcomes where past forecasts exist.
Compare modelled valuation signals with subsequent one-year, three-year and five-year total returns where sufficient point-in-time data exists.
Compare any hypothetical strategy with an appropriate total-return benchmark.
Include dividends and reasonable transaction-cost assumptions in hypothetical strategy returns.
Account for delisted, merged, suspended or otherwise unavailable securities to reduce survivorship bias.
Report the number of observations, coverage gaps and limitations of each backtest.

historical_model_validation.interpretation: Historical performance does not prove future predictive power. Report results as diagnostics and avoid tuning assumptions solely to maximise historical returns.

model_governance.change_log: Log changes to valuation formulas, peer groups, source data, assumptions and manual overrides. Preserve original raw observations. Do not claim a model or test is validated unless it has actually been run.
model_governance.confidence_reporting: Keep data confidence separate from valuation confidence. Define the components of any confidence label; do not create an unexplained weighted confidence score. Report data coverage, input freshness, model sensitivity and uncertainty explicitly.
model_governance.recalculation_check: Confirm that changes to user inputs recalculate dependent formulas and charts. Provide a documented reset process. Flag calculation mode, broken references, external links and formula errors.

implementation_sequence.phase: Source feasibility and data architecture Inventory required datasets, official holdings, prices, company filings and data access constraints. Create the security registry, source log, raw-data tables, data completeness checks and governance log. Do not build large valuation dashboards before confirming the availability and structure of data.

One complete bank valuation path Build the full HDFC Bank model, including historicals, forecasts, Residual Income valuation, DDM, relative valuation, sensitivity analysis, scenario controls and key charts. Independently check its formulas and source data.

One end-to-end actual fund calculation Select a security confirmed to exist in one selected fund's actual portfolio. Link its validated valuation to the fund's holdings table, calculate its weighted adjustment, roll the result into modelled intrinsic value per unit and test user-controlled price scenarios. Reconcile and document the method.

Scale across initial companies and funds Replicate the validated banking template for the other banks. Build the separate Max Financial insurance valuation. Import and independently validate both Direct Plan Growth portfolios, covering all material holdings.

Sector and industry valuation templates Add sector-specific valuation engines required by the actual fund constituents, including IT, consumer, metals, defence, industrials and other sectors. Do not build unused sector templates in preference to valuing actual material holdings.

Portfolio controls, performance and dynamic charts Implement actual holdings mode, custom allocation mode, market-price shocks, fundamental assumption scenarios, fair-value bias, absolute price overrides, target rebalancing, benchmark returns, risk metrics and formula-driven charts.

Historical validation and governance Run formula tests, historical diagnostics, data-completeness checks, price/date reconciliation and model-governance checks. Provide a source report, missing-data report, executed-test report, README and explicit limitations.

completion_criteria.criterion: Seven dedicated company valuation worksheets exist and link to the shared security registry and summary outputs.
The two Direct Plan Growth schemes have independent, source-backed constituent tables that can be updated without redesigning the workbook.
All material holdings across both funds have a valuation status and an appropriate valuation method or an explicit missing-data warning.
User-controlled market-price shocks, fair-value bias percentages and absolute scenario prices operate independently and recalculate linked portfolio outputs.
The workbook distinguishes actual official NAV, estimated fair NAV, scenario market NAV and hypothetical rebalanced portfolio value.
Sector allocation, growth, earnings, valuation multiples, peer comparisons, sensitivity analyses and fund NAV scenarios are represented through functioning Excel charts.
Every chart is linked to real formula outputs or sourced data, not static images.
The workbook includes source traceability, missing-data warnings, valuation coverage and executed validation results.
A new security from any supported sector can be added and incorporated into the correct fund-level calculation without rewriting the NAV engine.
Official NAV, modelled intrinsic value per unit, scenario market NAV and hypothetical rebalanced portfolio value are clearly separated throughout.
Market-price shock, fundamental assumption change, manual fair-value bias and absolute scenario price are independent controls with separate outputs.
The data-feasibility audit identifies available, missing, stale, derived, third-party and user-entered data before the model is declared complete.
A complete end-to-end test has been executed from one company's valuation through an actual fund holding to the estimated intrinsic value per unit.
Fund performance versus its stated benchmark, rolling returns, risk measures, fees and common holdings are included where reliable data is available.
Historical model testing is point-in-time-aware and reports look-ahead bias, survivorship bias, forecast errors, sample sizes and limitations.
Every key assumption and manual override is traceable through a model-governance log with original value, revised value, reason and date.

project_specification.final_instruction:
First inspect all supplied files and identify which required sources are available and which are missing. Produce the data-feasibility audit before building valuation outputs. Then build the workbook in the ordered phases.
The first acceptance test is one fully validated bank valuation linked to an actual holding in one of the two actual Direct Plan Growth funds, followed by a working fund-level modelled intrinsic value calculation and independently adjustable market-price and fair-value scenarios.
Make a best effort to deliver a functioning, formula-driven Excel workbook with auditable calculations and clear documentation. Do not fabricate data to create the appearance of completeness. If a live data source, consensus estimate or portfolio disclosure cannot be accessed, leave the affected field explicitly unpopulated, record the gap and explain its impact.
The result must allow the user to trace each estimated mutual-fund fair NAV back through the fund's actual holdings, sector and company valuations, model assumptions, market-price scenarios and source documents.
